Done — syntax verified, module exports `buildPlane` cleanly.

**What I changed:** Added a complete 747 landing-gear assembly to `plane.js` — the one feature both my own image inspection and the Claude judge track confirmed was entirely absent (mean 0/10, every view). Nothing else was moved or resized.

**Why this fix:** I opened the contact sheet plus views 2 and 8 myself: the model has no gear at all, while the side-profile reference photo (side.png) shows the 747 gear-down in flight and the three-view gives the exact bogie layout. Gemma's weakest (window lines) was already targeted last iteration and improved 0.43→3.14, so gear was the largest untouched gap — and it's purely additive under the belly, so the two views already scoring ≥7 (right-profile 8.69, rear 7.36) keep their silhouettes intact.

**The geometry (all Cylinder/Box primitives, ~27 meshes):**
- **Nose gear:** a thin strut at x=23 (~12% aft of the nose tip), embedded 0.3 into the hull, with two r=0.45 wheels astride it — the rubric's "two-wheel nose strut".
- **Four main bogies** in the real 747 arrangement: a body pair near the centerline (z=±1.8, strut tops embedded into the curved hull bottom at y=−2.4) and a wing pair outboard (z=±5.5, struts reaching up into the wing underside), with the body pair slightly aft of the wing pair. Each bogie is a strut + beam + four wheels (2 axles × 2), matching the "four multi-wheel main bogies (two under the body, two under the wings)" 10-anchor.
- **Craftsmanship guarded:** strut tops embed into hull/wing, strut bottoms embed into the bogie beams, wheel inner faces overlap the beams — nothing floats, no coplanar faces to z-fight. Wheel bottoms (y≈−5.45) clear the engine nacelles (bottoms −3.15) and sit level like the gear-down reference.

Wheel axles run along Z per the frozen orientation contract (nose +X, up +Y, span Z), and the file stays a self-contained ES module with the exact `export function buildPlane(THREE)` signature — no new geometry types beyond th
